'''Nadeschda Nikolayevna Gernet''' {{efn|Also cited as Nadezhda.<ref name=":4"/><ref name="dnb"/><ref name=":2"/>}} ({{langx|ru|Надежда Николаевна Гернет|Nadezhda Nikolayevna Gernet}}; April 18, 1877 – January 1, 1943) was a Russian mathematician, [[Academic staff|academic]], and the second Russian woman to earn a doctorate.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=gernet.nadeschda|title=zbMATH - the first resource for mathematics|website=zbmath.org|access-date=2019-07-08}}</ref><ref name="dnb">{{Cite web|url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=nid=116589442|title=Katalog der Deutschen Nationalbibliothek|website=portal.dnb.de|access-date=2019-07-08}}</ref><ref name=mr/><ref name=":1" /> Gernet extended the [[calculus of variations]] to further functions on the basis developed by her instructor, [[David Hilbert]], and was one of the first to include inequalities in the calculus of variations.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" />

== Life and career ==
Gernet was born on April 18, 1877 in [[Simbirsk]] (now Ulyanovsk), to Nikolai V. Gernet, a state councillor and his wife Nadezhda.<ref name=":4" /><ref name="dnb"/><ref name=":0" />

In the spring of 1894, Gernet graduated from high school in Simbirsk with a gold medal.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=j74UAQAAIAAJ&pg=GBS.PT2|title=Untersuchung zur Variationsrechnung: Ueber eine neue Methode in der Variationsrechnung|last=Gernet|first=Nadeschda|date=1902|publisher=Druck der Dietrich'schen Universitäts-Buchdruckerei (W. F. Kaestner)|contribution=Lebenslauf|language=de}}</ref> That fall, she began her higher education at [[Bestuzhev Courses|Women's University of Saint Petersburg]], where she took science and math-related classes.<ref name=":0" /> She was the first to graduate from the Women's University of Petersburg.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rbth.com/history/329326-russia-first-female-education|title=What Russia's first female 'college' looked like (PHOTOS)|last=Guzeva|first=Alexandra|date=2018-10-16|website=www.rbth.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-09}}</ref> Gernet's academic interests included, but were not limited to, mathematics, astronomy, and physics.<ref name=":0" /> 

In 1902, Gernet received a PhD for her thesis ''Untersuchung zur Variationsrechnung'' ("On One New Method in the Variation of Calculus"), written at the [[University of Göttingen]]<ref name=":0" /> in Germany. She was the second female doctoral candidate to study under the instruction of David Hilbert,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=7350|title=Nadeschda Gernet - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-07-08}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/gernet.htm|title=Nadezhda Gernet|website=www.agnesscott.edu|access-date=2019-07-08}}</ref> [[Anne Bosworth]] having been the first. In her thesis, Gernet extended the calculus of variations and generalized Hilbert's independence theorem to the case of two unknown functions.<ref name=":0" /> After defending her thesis, Gernet became the second woman in Russia to hold a doctorate, and the ''[[International Catalogue of Scientific Literature]]: First Volume'' indexed Gernet's book within the same year.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qSdLAAAAYAAJ|title=International Catalogue of Scientific Literature: Mathematics. A|date=1902|publisher=International Council|language=en|page=71}}</ref>  

As her German doctorate was not recognized in Russia, in 1915 Gernet submitted her thesis ''On the Fundamental Simplest Problems of Variation Calculus'' to [[Moscow University]] in order to obtain a Russian master's degree which would also enable her to take up a university position.<ref name=mr/><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Mw6JMdZQO-wC&pg=PA259|title=Mathematics of the 19th Century: Function Theory According to Chebyshev Ordinary Differential Equations Calculus of Variations Theory of Finite Differences|last1=Kolmogorov|first1=A. N.|last2=Yushkevich|first2=A. P.|author-link=Andrey Kolmogorov|author-link2=Adolph P. Yushkevich|date=1998-03-24|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9783764358457|pages=259|language=en}}</ref> Gernet included a summary of the past achievements within the field of calculus of variations, and she was the first to attempt the inclusion of inequalities in the calculus of variations.<ref name=":3" />
[[File:CimetierePetersbourg5.JPG|thumb|[[Smolensky Lutheran Cemetery]]]]

After defending her master's thesis and obtaining her degree with outstanding results from [[Moscow University]], Gernet began her teaching career at the [[Saint Petersburg State University]] where she taught until 1929.<ref name=mr>{{cite web|url=https://math.ru/history/people/gernet_NN|title=Гернет Надежда Николаевна |publisher=math.ru|access-date=1 August 2019 |language=ru}}</ref> Her curriculum focused on educating female students in the Women's Higher Courses.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> Soon after, she began teaching at the [[Leningrad Polytechnic Institute]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ul.aif.ru/istoria/simbiryanka_nadezhda_gernet_-_vtoraya_posle_sofi_kovalevskoy|title=Симбирянка Надежда Гернет - вторая после Софьи Ковалевской|publisher=AIF.RU: Аргументы и Факты" № 21|date= 23 May 2018|access-date=1 August 2019 |language=ru}}</ref> On January 1, 1943, Gernet died in [[Leningrad]] (now St.&nbsp;Petersburg) during the blockades of the [[Siege of Leningrad]] and was buried in the [[Smolensky Lutheran Cemetery]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m_WRu23Ut6sC&pg=PA211|title=Translations. Ser. 2, 159. Proceedings of the St. Petersburg Mathematical Society. - 2|last=Research|first=United States Office of Naval|date=1994-11-22|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=9780821895931|language=en}}</ref>

Gernet's publications raised new discussions, and her work encouraged further development in the calculus of variations.<ref name=":3" />

== Publications ==
*''On One New Method in the Variation of Calculus''<ref name=":0" />
*''On the Fundamental Simplest Problems of Variation Calculus''<ref name=":3" />
